title: The home screen, three ways in the nutrition material
question: All three are built, not drawn: the areas, their titles and their icons are lifted out of the app, and the material is exactly what the nutrition screen settled into - ground #e9e7e3, a raised disc whose glyph carries the colour and throws it onto the ground behind, no borders, and the app's own bottom bar. They differ only in topology. Pick one and we refine it.

options.label: The fan
options.thesis: The arc you kept from the start, rebuilt in the new material: eight lit discs around a pressed hub that holds what the day has in it. The quietest of the three.
options.viewport: Greeting, the arc, the hub, the bar.
options.risk: It has no words. Eight labels on an arc this short collapse into each other - I tried - so a first-time reader cannot tell what any disc is. The fix is the hub naming whatever is touched, but the problem is real and not decoration.

options.label: The grid
options.thesis: Eight raised tiles, two to a row, each with its disc and its name. The one a person can read on the first open.
options.risk: It treats the eight areas as equals, and they are not: the reflection is the spine and here it is one tile of eight.

options.label: The column
options.thesis: סיום יום at the top as a lit bar - the one lit thing on the screen, exactly like the write-line in nutrition - and the other seven as rows in the same rhythm as the meal pills.
options.viewport: The lit reflection bar, seven rows, the bar.
options.risk: The most ordinary shape of the three, and it gives up the fan - which you said early on you liked.
